short: Money spent acquiring or improving long-lived assets.
seoTitle: Capital Expenditure — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Capital expenditure is money spent acquiring or improving long-lived assets — a new outlet fit-out, kitchen equipment, a delivery vehicle.
definition: Capital expenditure is money spent acquiring or improving long-lived assets — a new outlet fit-out, kitchen equipment, a delivery vehicle. It is capitalised on the balance sheet rather than expensed in one period.
bodyHtml:
Why Capital Expenditure matters

Capex decisions commit cash for years and are largely irreversible. They belong to a payback and return analysis, not to a monthly expense conversation.

Capital Expenditure formula

Payback period = Initial investment ÷ Annual cash inflow generated

Compare against the asset's useful life before committing.

How Capital Expenditure works in practice

Evaluate each with a payback period and, for larger commitments, an ROI. Remember that capex consumes cash immediately while only depreciation appears in the P&L, which is why a profitable year can still be a cash-poor one.

faq.question: Is a repair capex or an expense?
faq.answer: Routine repairs are expenses; improvements that extend life or capacity are capitalised.

faq.question: Why does capex not appear in my P&L?
faq.answer: Only the depreciation does. The cash outflow shows up in the cash flow statement instead.
